naslov: Are We Contributing to Allah's Religion?

segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين. قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون. أما بعد. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him),

upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Abu Hurayrah, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu (may Allah be pleased with him), narrates

that a woman, during the time the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, lived in Medina, came every day to the mosque of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, cleaned it, looked after it, [unclear].
And so every, every day – a woman who was not an Arab, a woman from the land of Africa, though some say she was an Arab – a woman who had no one.
The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, would see her every day looking after the mosque, cleaning the mosque. And then for some time she was not there.

That woman is not there, she is not there to clean, to look after the mosque. For several days now. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, called his companions and asked them: “Do you know where this woman who looks after the mosque is? What has happened to her? Has something happened, is she ill?”
They said: “O Prophet, she passed away a few days ago. She passed away late, so we did not,” they said, “want to wake you, to disturb you because of that woman.

We,” they said, “prayed the janazah (funeral prayer) for her and buried her.” And the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, became angry and said: “Take me to her grave, quickly take me to her grave.” So they took him to her grave, and the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, [unclear] prayed the janazah and supplicated for her.
Dear brothers, we see the example of this woman. This woman did not have Shari'ah knowledge with which to teach others, nor was she rich so as to give in the way of Allah.
She was not physically able [unclear] to fight in the way of Allah, but for Allah's religion she did, or kept doing, as much as she could.
Do we sometimes ask ourselves what we have done for Allah's religion, do we sometimes put that question to ourselves? Let us be honest.
Are we ready, tomorrow, when we stand before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to give an answer to our Lord about what we have done for the religion?
What have we done for His religion, which He sent to us as a trust?
Do we have an answer? By Allah, [unclear] of us knows the answer. Dear brothers, we would like to change the condition of the community, but only through messages.

Only through social networks. We would like to change the condition of the community, and by Allah some even that of the ummah, yet we are not capable of putting those slippers back in their place in the ablution room.

That you have about a hundred people who come to the mosque, yet you don't have one or two who will, let's say, clean the ablution room. That you have about a hundred members of a group, yet you don't have one or two who will share the mosque's activities – some lecture taking place in the mosque – something good, out of all that good.

So, the condition of a community cannot be changed in that way, until every individual becomes aware of his role, becomes aware of his condition, and until every individual takes responsibility. That is how a community is built, that is how a community is raised up.

We have a situation where one says: “I'm not interested,” this one says: “I'm not interested,” that third one says: “I'm not interested,” and no one is interested. Because, if our condition is a catastrophe… And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will not improve our condition, as He says: “Innallaha la yughayyiru ma bi qawmin hatta yughayyiru ma bi anfusihim” – indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change themselves, until we start to change ourselves.

First from himself, let him change himself. A person would like to change the condition of the community, yet he is not at the fajr prayer. You must change yourself, come to fajr, come to the mosque, improve your relationship with your wife, with your parents, with your neighbors, and then set the others right. We must change, dear brothers.

We cannot live every day in some uncertainty: “This happened, that happened.” You see for yourselves how every day the situation is getting worse and worse, worse and worse. That is why it is time, dear brothers, for us to come to our senses, first of all to return [unclear], and after that to all the moral values that make a person a human being.

I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to improve our condition, that we may be among those who will know how to give an answer, and be able to give an answer, to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, on the Day of Judgment. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive us our sins and the sins of our parents.

I ask Him, the Exalted, to unite us in Jannah (Paradise). Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin. Barakallahu li wa lakum fil-Qur'an al-'azim, wa nafa'ani wa iyyakum bima fihi min al-ayati wadh-dhikr al-hakim. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum… [unclear]
